P2300.d: P2300 reports that the control line to ignition coil A is pulled towards ground. GM, Saab and VW assign coil A to cylinder 1.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire and rough running on cylinder 1
Noticeable loss of power
Fuel to cylinder 1 cut off by the engine module
c: Coil A (cylinder 1) with an internal fault pulling the control input to ground
Control wire of coil A chafed through and touching engine ground
Water or corrosion in the coil A connector
Engine module driver or software fault (FCA 2023: PCM reflash)

P2301.d: P2301 is the mirror image of P2300: the control line of coil A, i.e. cylinder 1, carries voltage at a moment when the engine module is trying to pull it low.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 1 misfires, engine shakes at idle
Jerking and loss of power under load
c: Coil A with an internal short feeding supply voltage onto the control input
Control wire of coil A rubbing against a 12 V line in the harness
Broken control line or loose pin (counts as P2301 on Saab Trionic 8)
Faulty output stage in the engine module

P2302.d: P2302 looks at the high-voltage side of coil A – the secondary winding, the boot and the spark plug of cylinder 1 – rather than at the control line covered by P2300 and P2301. Only a few makers use it.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 1, often together with P0301
Rough idle and hesitation
c: Worn or fouled spark plug in cylinder 1, gap too wide
Cracked coil boot letting the spark jump to the cylinder head
Secondary winding of coil A breaking down
Ion-sense evaluation in the PCM (FCA 18-069-16: PCM replaced)

P2303.d: P2303 tells you that the trigger wire of coil B – cylinder 2 in GM, Saab and VW documentation – has found a path to ground. On the Saab 9-5 2.0 turbo (GM LDK engine, 2010) the check runs continuously below 6,000 rpm with 9–18 V on the ignition feed and sets after 4 s of uninterrupted short or 50 s added up; as a Type B code it turns on the MIL only after a second failing trip.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 2
Engine runs on fewer cylinders, less power
c: Coil B (cylinder 2) faulty, pulling the control line low
Insulation damage on the coil B control wire touching ground
PCM software assigning the code to the wrong cylinder (Ford Bronco, FCA 2.0 turbo)

P2304.d: P2304 means the control line of coil B (cylinder 2) is held at too high a voltage – usually a short to a supply line, sometimes an internal coil fault. In VW's 2014 tables a primary control circuit counts as high once its signal voltage exceeds about 5.1–7.0 V, while the low code reacts to a current above 24 mA; the Touareg six-cylinder petrol table (engine code CGRA) names the coils directly by cylinder number.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 2 misfiring
Shaking at idle, weak acceleration
c: Coil B control wire shorted to a voltage-carrying line
Internal fault in coil B or its built-in driver
Engine module fault (Polaris Slingshot 2026: ECM replaced)
Interrupted control line on systems that report it here (Saab Trionic 8)

P2305.d: P2305 is about coil B's output side: the secondary winding, the connection to the plug and the spark plug of cylinder 2. Where a maker uses it, the module does not just watch whether the coil was switched, but whether a usable spark happened.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 2, sometimes only under load
Rough running, raised fuel consumption
c: Spark plug of cylinder 2 worn, oily or with the wrong gap
Coil B boot cracked or damp, spark leaking away
Faulty ion-current evaluation in the PCM

P2306.d: With P2306 the engine module has seen the output for coil C, cylinder 3 at GM, Saab and VW, dragged down to ground. Ford explains where such a fault can sit on engines whose coils carry their own driver: the coil-driver chip in the PCM watches current and voltage at its output, so the culprit may be the PCM, the harness, the plug-in connection at the coil or the driver electronics inside the coil – but not the windin
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 3
Uneven idle, possibly cylinder shut-off
c: Driver electronics inside coil C defective
Coil C control wire grounded through chafing or a pinched harness
Corroded or bent pins at the coil C connector

P2307.d: P2307 sets when the coil C control line, cylinder 3 in most layouts, is shorted to a voltage source. On GM's 3.6-litre LLT V6 (2008) the check is a continuity test against voltage that runs below 6,000 rpm with the battery between 9.99 and 18.1 V and needs 4 s at a stretch or 50 s in total.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 3 misfires
Power loss, engine runs rough
c: Coil C control wire touching a battery-voltage line
Coil C with an internal short to its supply
Code filed against the wrong cylinder by PCM software (Ford Bronco SSM 52342)
Broken control wire on systems reporting opens here (Saab Trionic 8)

P2308.d: P2308 points at the high-voltage path of coil C, normally cylinder 3: winding, boot and plug. The code is uncommon.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 3 with P0303 stored
Engine runs rough
c: Spark plug of cylinder 3 worn or fouled
Boot of coil C leaking high voltage
FCA vans built 27 July–11 September 2015: PCM fault (bulletin 18-069-16)

P2309.d: P2309 stands for a grounded control lead to coil D – cylinder 4, which on a four-cylinder engine is the last coil in the row. In 2023 FCA released bulletins 18-022-23 and 18-023-23 for the Alfa Romeo Giulia and Stelvio with the 280 hp 2.0 turbo: P2300-00, P2303-00, P2306-00 and P2309-00 could set together with an EVAP purge code, and the remedy was PCM software rather than parts.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 4
Auto stop-start no longer works (Ford)
Reduced power
c: PCM software fault setting several coil low codes (FCA 2.0 turbo 2023)
Damaged harness section carrying several coil lines
Poor contact or moisture at the coil D connector

P230A.d: P230A belongs to a second series of cylinder imbalance codes. P219C reports that cylinder 1 runs a mixture unlike the others; P230A goes a step further and says the balancing function has already moved the fuel correction for cylinder 1 to its end stop without evening it out.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 1
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 1 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 1
Valve of cylinder 1 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 1

P230B.d: P230B singles out cylinder 2: its individual fuel correction has reached the limit during cylinder balancing and the imbalance remains. Audi is one of the few makers whose use of the code is on record.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 2
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 2 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 2
Valve of cylinder 2 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Calibration error in the cylinder assignment (Audi 2.0 TFSI Gen 3, bulletin 2060348)

P230C.d: P230C is the balance-limit code for cylinder 3. On three-cylinder engines this is the last cylinder of the row; on fours and larger engines it sits further inside.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 3
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 3 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 3
Valve of cylinder 3 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 3

P230D.d: P230D flags cylinder 4, so the engine needs at least four cylinders. The balancing function has run the individual fuel trim for that cylinder to its limit and the mixture still deviates.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 4
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 4 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 4
Valve of cylinder 4 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 4

P230E.d: P230E concerns cylinder 5 and is genuine only on engines with five or more cylinders, such as inline fives, sixes and V8s. The balancing logic has exhausted the individual fuel trim for cylinder 5.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 5
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 5 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 5
Valve of cylinder 5 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Calibration error in the cylinder assignment (Audi 2.0 TFSI Gen 3, bulletin 2060348)

P230F.d: P230F is the balance-limit code for cylinder 6 and can only appear on engines with six or more cylinders, inline sixes, V6 units and larger. On a V6, cylinder 6 shares its bank and front oxygen sensor with two others, so its individual trim has to be estimated from that bank signal or from crankshaft speed.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 6
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 6 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 6
Valve of cylinder 6 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 6

P2310.d: P2310 sets when the coil D control line, belonging to cylinder 4, carries voltage while the engine module tries to switch it to ground. Saab's Trionic 8 (9-3, 2003) uses a 2 V limit held for over 1 s and evaluates cylinder 4 together with cylinder 2 for its ion-based combustion signal; the injector of the affected cylinder is shut off.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 4 misfiring, injector shut off
Rough idle
c: Coil D control wire shorted to a voltage source
Interrupted line reported as high on Saab Trionic 8
Defective driver in the engine module

P2311.d: P2311 concerns the secondary side of coil D, usually cylinder 4. The secondary winding has thousands of turns of fine wire and delivers roughly 15–40 kV, so insulation that is merely tired can let the spark escape to ground instead of crossing the plug gap.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 4, worse in damp weather or under load
Flashing MIL at heavy misfire
c: Aged insulation in coil D or its boot letting the spark leak to ground
Spark plug of cylinder 4 worn, gap grown
Oil in the plug well softening the boot

P2312.d: P2312 is the first code of this series that only engines with five or more cylinders can set: it flags the control lead of coil E, i.e. cylinder 5, as shorted to ground.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 5
Rough running, less power
c: Short in the coil supply shared by one bank (Saab LAU: coils 1, 3, 5)
Coil E control wire chafed against ground
Wrong cylinder assignment in PCM software (Ford SSM 52455)

P2313.d: P2313 reports that the control line of coil E, cylinder 5, is shorted to positive, and therefore needs an engine with at least five cylinders. Saab spells out the conditions for its 9-5 2.8 V6 (LAU, 2011): engine running at 400–5,000 rpm with 10–18 V, a check on every crank revolution once 20 have passed, and a fault after more than 4 s or 30 s in total; P2313 is a Type B code.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 5 misfiring
Hesitation and jerking under load
c: Aftermarket device spliced into the coil wiring (Saab LAU note)
Coil E internally shorted to supply
Coil E control wire touching a 12 V line
PCM cylinder mapping error (Ford Bronco 3.0, TSB 24-2406)

P2314.d: P2314 reports a fault on the high-voltage side of coil E, which only five-cylinder and larger engines have; it normally fires cylinder 5. The control line may be perfectly sound; what failed is the energy reaching the plug or the combustion that should follow.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 5
Rough idle, slight vibration
c: Spark plug of cylinder 5 worn or fouled
Coil E secondary winding or boot damaged
PCM fault on FCA vans from the 2015 build window

P2315.d: P2315 indicates that the switching line of coil F – cylinder 6 – is grounded, so six-, eight- and larger engines only. Several makers name the cylinder outright: VW's 2014 Touareg table for the six-cylinder petrol engine CGRA speaks of the ignition coil of cylinder 6, Saab's 9-5 2.8 V6 of coil 6, and GM's 2008 3.6 V6 (LLT) lists P2315 with the other five ground-short codes.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 6
Engine shakes, power down
c: Fault in the bank 2 coil supply affecting coils 2, 4 and 6 (Saab LAU)
Coil F control wire chafed to ground near the rear of the engine

P2316.d: P2316 means the coil F control line, cylinder 6, sits at a voltage it should not have while the module switches it – a short to supply or a fault inside the coil. In VW's 2014 Touareg tables the high threshold is a signal voltage above about 5.1–7.0 V.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 6, P0306 may also be stored
Intermittent stumbling
c: Coil F control wire shorted to a supply line
Intermittent contact in the harness near coil F

P2317.d: P2317 concerns the high-voltage side of coil F, which serves cylinder 6 on engines with six or more cylinders. With coil-on-plug designs there is no separate lead any more – Ford notes that individual coils did away with plug wires – so a secondary fault lies in the coil, its boot or the plug.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 6
Uneven running, especially under load
c: Spark plug of cylinder 6 worn or wrongly gapped
Coil F boot cracked or contaminated

P2318.d: P2318 says the command wire of coil G, cylinder 7, is touching ground, so it only occurs on V8, V10 or V12 engines. GM's 2019 table for the 5.3-litre L84 truck V8 lists it as a Type B code (50 of 63 failed samples, battery above 11 V, MIL after two trips).
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 7
V8 runs noticeably rough, power reduced
c: Water or corrosion at the coil G connector
Control wire of coil G grounded by heat or chafing damage
PCM cylinder mapping error on Ford 6.8/7.3 (SSM 52455)

P2319.d: P2319 sets when the coil G control line, belonging to cylinder 7 of a V8 or larger engine, shows a short to voltage. GM's 2019 tables include it for the LT5 Corvette V8 as a Type B code with 50 of 63 failed samples.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 7 shut off for periods of 30 s (Ford)
Rough running and loss of power
c: Coil G control wire shorted to a supply line
Code assigned to the wrong cylinder by PCM software (Ford SSM 52455)

P231A.d: P231A takes the series to cylinder 7; since P2310 to P2319 are ignition coil codes, the versions for cylinders 7 to 12 start at P231A. Only engines with eight or more cylinders can set it.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 7
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 7 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 7
Valve of cylinder 7 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression

P231B.d: P231B is the balance-limit code for cylinder 8, the last cylinder of a V8 and an inner one on V10 and V12 engines. The fuel trim for that cylinder has hit its stop while balancing.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 8
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 8 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 8
Valve of cylinder 8 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 8

P231C.d: P231C points to cylinder 9 and therefore exists only on ten- and twelve-cylinder engines, a small group of mostly high-performance and heavy-duty petrol units. The balancing logic has pushed the fuel trim for cylinder 9 to its limit.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 9
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 9 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 9
Valve of cylinder 9 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 9

P231D.d: P231D is the cylinder 10 code of the balance-limit series. On a V10 it marks the last cylinder, on a V12 one of the inner ones; smaller engines cannot set it.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 10
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 10 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 10
Valve of cylinder 10 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 10

P231E.d: P231E belongs to cylinder 11 and can only come from twelve-cylinder engines, V12 or W12. The per-cylinder fuel trim for cylinder 11 sits at its limit during balancing.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 11
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 11 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 11
Valve of cylinder 11 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 11

P231F.d: P231F closes the balance-limit series at cylinder 12, the last cylinder of a twelve-cylinder engine. It says the balancing routine has used up the fuel trim for that cylinder without matching it to the rest.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle, possibly misfire on cylinder 12
Higher fuel consumption or exhaust smell
c: Injector of cylinder 12 delivering too much or too little (deposits, wear)
Air leak at the intake port or injector seal of cylinder 12
Valve of cylinder 12 not sealing (worn seat or guide), low compression
Poor contact at the connector of injector 12

P2320.d: P2320 points at the high-voltage half of coil G, normally the coil on cylinder 7, so only engines with seven or more cylinders can log it. FCA is the maker on record: STAR case S2118000002 from March 2021 for the 2020–2021 Ram 1500 names P2320 as coil 7 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire felt on cylinder 7, often with P0307
Engine shakes at idle or under load
c: Coil 7 connector not fully seated or latched (FCA)
Spark plug of cylinder 7 worn, fouled or with wrong gap
Coil G secondary winding or boot breaking down
Ion-current evaluation in the PCM faulty

P2321.d: With P2321 the engine module has seen the switching line of coil H pulled to ground; on a V8 coil H is the final one, on a V10 it is number eight. GM's 2019 tables, which label the code as cylinder 8, carry it for the LT5 Corvette and the L84 5.3-litre truck engine: a Type B fault after 50 bad readings in 63 samples taken every 100 ms with the system above 11 V.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 8 misfires or drops out
Rough idle and weaker pulling power
c: Water ingress or corrosion in the coil H connector (GM PIP5147)
Coil H control wire chafed through to ground
Coil driver stage in the engine module damaged

P2322.d: P2322 is the counterpart to P2321: the coil H control line, cylinder 8 on most V8 layouts, reads as if it were tied to voltage. GM monitors it the same way on the 2019 LT5 and L84 engines, as a Type B code, flagged once 50 of 63 samples fail.
s: Check engine light on
One cylinder repeatedly shut off for about 30 s (Ford)
Noticeable vibration and loss of power
c: Coil H control wire shorted to a voltage-carrying line
PCM assigns the code to the wrong cylinder (Ford SSM 52455/52342)
Output stage in the engine module faulty

P2323.d: P2323 concerns the spark side of coil H, the coil on cylinder 8. It is the last code of FCA's ion-sensing series: STAR case S2118000002 (2021) for the 2020–2021 Ram 1500 reads it as coil 8 secondary circuit with insufficient ionization, and an older FCA parts review lists it together with the cylinder misfire codes P0301–P0308.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 8 misfire, frequently stored with P0308
Rough running when accelerating
c: Coil 8 connector loose or not latched (FCA)
Worn or fouled spark plug on cylinder 8
Coil H boot cracked or tracking to the head

P2324.d: Coil I is the ninth coil, so P2324 only appears on ten- or twelve-cylinder petrol engines. The documented user is Ford: its OBD system summaries (2012 and 2020–2023) group P2324 with the other codes for a coil driver shorted to ground, monitored continuously from 200 rpm with the battery between 11 and 16 V, and Ford's 2014 code interpretation list marks it as a MIL code.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 9 cuts out, rough running
Reduced towing or climbing power
c: Coil I control wire grounded on the engine or exhaust side
Moisture or corroded pins at the coil I plug
PCM coil driver for cylinder 9 failed

P2325.d: P2325 flags a short to voltage on the trigger line of coil I, the ninth ignition output. Ford is again the only maker that lists it publicly: in its OBD summaries P2325 sits among the codes for a coil driver shorted high, and the 2014 Ford code list shows it as a MIL-lighting code checked with the engine running.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 9 drops out in roughly 30 s cycles
Uneven idle and vibration
c: Coil I control wire touching a 12 V feed
PCM driver stage for coil I faulty

P2326.d: P2326 would report a fault in the high-voltage output of coil I – coil, boot or plug of the ninth cylinder. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 9 (P0309)
Hesitation under heavy load
c: Spark plug on cylinder 9 worn or bridged
Coil I boot perforated or oil-soaked

P2327.d: P2327 is the highest ground-side coil code Ford publishes: its driver short-circuit-low list in the 2012 and 2020–2023 OBD summaries runs from P2300 up to P2327 and stops there, matching a ten-coil engine such as the 6.8-litre Modular V10. Coil J serves the tenth cylinder in Ford's count.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 10 missing, engine shakes
Higher fuel consumption from cylinder shut-off cycles
c: Coil J (cylinder 10) failed with internal short
Coil J signal wire shorted to ground near the rear of the engine
Corroded or water-filled coil J connector
PCM driver for coil J defective

P2328.d: P2328 marks the end of Ford's published coil list: it is the last entry in the driver short-circuit-high group of the 2012 and 2020–2023 OBD summaries, and the 2014 Ford code list puts it directly before the evaporative codes with a MIL flag. It tells you the switching wire of coil J, the tenth coil, carries voltage where the driver expects a path to ground, or that the coil draws a current outside the allowed window
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 10 switched off at intervals
Engine runs rough and pulls weakly
c: Coil J control wire shorted to battery voltage
PCM output for coil J damaged

P2329.d: P2329 covers the secondary side of coil J, meaning the spark path to the plug of cylinder 10. No public manufacturer source assigns it.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 10 (P0310)
Jerking under acceleration, worse when damp
c: Carbon tracking on the coil J boot

P232A.d: P232A is stored by the engine module when the transmission control module has demanded that the engine be switched off. A TCM sends such a request over the vehicle network when it decides that keeping the engine running could harm the transmission or the vehicle, typically after a serious internal transmission or module fault; the root cause then sits as a separate code in the TCM.
s: Engine shuts off while driving or at idle
Engine cranks but does not stay running until the fault is cleared
Transmission warning and further codes in the TCM
c: Serious transmission fault detected by the TCM (stored there as its own code)
Disturbed CAN communication between TCM and engine module
Low battery voltage or poor supply/ground at the TCM
Mismatched or outdated TCM/engine software after repair or replacement

P232B.d: Common-rail diesels keep a small-quantity correction for every injector. During overrun fuel cut the module fires one injector alone with a tiny known amount (GM: about 1.5 mm³), judges the torque from crankshaft acceleration and records how much the energizing time has to change at each rail pressure level.
s: Check engine light on
Often no noticeable change; possibly louder combustion noise or rough idle
Possibly smoke or higher fuel consumption
c: Injector of cylinder 11 leaking or delivering too much at small quantities
Injector correction code not or wrongly entered after replacement
Disturbed crankshaft speed signal falsifying the torque evaluation

P232C.d: P232C is the upper-limit partner of P232B for injector A in cylinder 11. The small-quantity learning has found that this injector needs far more energizing time than the nominal map to produce the expected torque pulse, and the stored correction has hit its maximum at one or more rail pressure levels.
s: MIL on after two trips
Rough idle or uneven running at low load
Possibly harder starting or more smoke
c: Injector of cylinder 11 coked, worn or sticking (delivers too little)
Injector correction code missing or wrong after replacement
Poor fuel quality or contamination promoting deposits

P232D.d: The offset-learning codes for injector A of cylinders 1 to 10 sit at P02CC to P02DF; cylinders 11 and 12 were placed separately at P232B to P232E, and P232D is the lower limit for cylinder 12, the last cylinder of a V12. The engine module calibrates each injector in overrun with small test injections and crankshaft-acceleration feedback (GM: test quantity around 1.5 mm³, values kept per rail pressure level).
s: Check engine light on
Possibly harsher combustion noise or knocking at idle
Possibly more smoke or consumption
c: Injector of cylinder 12 leaking or opening early
Correction code not programmed after fitting a new injector
Crankshaft signal disturbed (tone wheel, sensor, flywheel)

P232E.d: P232E closes the row of injector A offset-learning codes: cylinder 12, upper limit. The learned extra energizing time for this injector has run to the top of its range for at least one rail pressure level, meaning the injector needs much longer activation than its nominal map to give the expected small-quantity torque – it under-delivers or opens late, often from coking or wear.
s: MIL on after two trips
Uneven idle, possibly harder starting
Often no other noticeable change
c: Injector of cylinder 12 coked or worn (delivers too little)
Injector correction code missing or wrong
High resistance in the injector wiring slowing the opening

P232F.d: P232F checks the downstream oxygen signal of bank 1 while fuel is cut on deceleration and the exhaust holds almost pure air. GM uses it on the 2023 6.6L L5P Duramax (Silverado HD, Sierra HD): the O2 value of sensor 2, the downstream NOx sensor, is compared with that of sensor 1 once the latter is stable in overrun; if the filtered difference leaves the window of +3.01 % to −3.18 %, a Type B fault is stored.
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in driving behaviour
MIL only after two trips with the fault (GM Type B)
c: Downstream sensor drifting or aged (on GM diesels the O2 signal of NOx sensor 2)
Exhaust leak near the downstream sensor
Damaged sensor wiring or connector (chafing, corrosion)
Leaking injector or upstream sensor fault distorting the overrun comparison

P2330.d: P2330 belongs to coil K, the eleventh coil, which only twelve-cylinder petrol engines have – V12 units such as those built by BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Lamborghini or Ferrari, or the VW group's W12. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; the published coil lists stop earlier (Ford at J, GM at H).
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 11 not firing
Slight roughness, often hard to feel on a V12
c: Coil K control wire damaged and grounded in the bank harness
Coil K driver in the engine module faulty

P2331.d: P2331 is the short-to-power version for coil K, cylinder 11 in a straightforward count. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; neither Ford nor GM, whose OBD descriptions explain the primary codes in detail, build engines with eleven or more coils.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 11 may be fuel-cut temporarily
Slightly uneven idle
c: Coil K signal wire shorted to a supply wire
Engine module output for coil K defective

P2332.d: P2332 reserves a code for trouble between coil K and the plug of cylinder 11. No manufacturer documents it publicly: the only published secondary-circuit series, FCA's ion-current codes, covers coils 1 to 8, and twelve-cylinder makers do not release their code lists.
s: Check engine light on
Misfire on cylinder 11 (P0311)
Faint vibration at idle
c: Oil in the plug well of cylinder 11
Spark plug of cylinder 11 worn out

P2333.d: P2333 is the ground-short code for coil L, the twelfth and final coil letter in the SAE scheme. It fits only V12 or W12 engines.
s: Check engine light on
One cylinder (usually 12) not firing
Mild roughness at idle
c: Coil L control wire chafed to ground
Damaged or corroded coil L connector
Coil L output stage in the engine module failed

P2334.d: P2334, the last primary-side coil code of the series, reports a short to voltage on the coil L trigger line. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; it can only occur on engines with twelve individual coils.
s: Check engine light on
Cylinder 12 intermittently dead
Hardly noticeable loss of smoothness
c: Coil L control wire shorted to a voltage source
Engine module output for coil L defective

P2335.d: P2335 closes the ignition coil block of J2012: a fault on the high-voltage side of coil L, the twelfth coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the reviewed ion-sensing or secondary-monitoring documents reaches past coil 8.
s: Check engine light on, possibly flashing with heavy misfire
Misfire on cylinder 12 (P0312)

P2336.d: The engine module listens to the knock sensors and assigns each vibration burst to the cylinder whose combustion falls into that crank-angle window, so it can retard spark on one cylinder alone. P2336 means the knock intensity attributed to cylinder 1 has exceeded the calibrated threshold.
s: Check engine light on
Knocking or pinging noise from the engine
Less power because spark is retarded
c: Engine damage from machining debris or casting sand (Stellantis 2.0L PHEV, bulletin 09-009-26)
Carbon deposits or hot spots in cylinder 1
Fuel with too low octane rating
Cylinder 1 running lean (injector delivering too little)

P2337.d: P2337 is the cylinder 2 entry of the per-cylinder knock series P2336–P2347. Using crank position, the engine module splits the knock sensor signal into one window per combustion event and compares the vibration level in cylinder 2's window with its threshold; above it the code is stored and spark for that cylinder is pulled back.
s: MIL on
Audible knocking, especially under load
Reduced power or sluggish acceleration
c: Internal damage from debris left in the engine (Stellantis 2.0L PHEV)
Deposits on piston or valves of cylinder 2
Wrong or worn spark plug in cylinder 2
Mechanical noise falling into cylinder 2's knock window

P2338.d: P2338 sets when the knock signal assigned to cylinder 3 rises above its threshold. Because one or two knock sensors serve several cylinders, the module relies on the crank-angle window to tell which cylinder knocked; a code for just one cylinder therefore suggests something local: carbon build-up, a hot spot, a lean-running injector, a wrong spark plug, or mechanical noise that happens to fall into that window.
s: Check engine light on
Pinging under acceleration
Noticeably less power
c: Carbon build-up or a hot spot in cylinder 3
Injector of cylinder 3 delivering too little (lean, hot combustion)
Engine damage from casting sand or chips (Stellantis 2.0L PHEV)
Knock sensor loose or wrongly torqued, picking up noise

P2339.d: P2339 covers cylinder 4. On a four-cylinder engine this is the last cylinder of the series, which is why Stellantis bulletin 09-009-26 lists exactly P2336 to P2339 for the 2.0L turbo PHEV (sales code ECX, Jeep Wrangler 4xe 2024–2025, Grand Cherokee 2023–2025): any of the four codes with the MIL on, often together with a knocking noise, qualifies for an engine replacement under an extended warranty because of machinin
s: MIL on
Knocking noise from the engine compartment
Reduced power
c: Machining debris or casting sand damaging the engine (Stellantis bulletin 09-009-26)
Low-octane fuel or high intake temperature

P233A.d: Fuel pressure regulator C is a third pressure actuator that only a few high-pressure systems have; which valve carries the letter is up to the manufacturer. GM's 2025 diesel table 25OBDG04B assigns C to a second fuel metering unit valve on the pump, driven by the ECM through a high-side and a low-side switch.
s: Check engine light on in the first trip
Rail pressure deviates, hesitation or reduced power
Possibly hard starting or stalling
c: Valve connector loose, corroded or a terminal pushed back
Engine harness wire broken where it rubs on brackets or clamps
Coil of the metering valve interrupted
Output driver in the engine control module faulty

P233B.d: P233B points to the ground side of fuel pressure regulator C: the line between valve and low-side driver has contact with ground. In GM's 2025 diesel table 25OBDG04B, regulator C is the second fuel metering unit valve, and the ECM checks this line while the driver is switched off.
s: Check engine light on immediately
Rail pressure too high or unstable, rough running
Reduced engine power possible
c: Insulation of the control wire worn through against engine or bracket
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the valve connector
Metering valve winding shorted to its housing
Low-side driver in the engine control module damaged

P233C.d: With P233C the ECM sees the control line of fuel pressure regulator C pulled towards battery voltage. GM's 2025 diesel table 25OBDG04B runs this test while the low-side driver of the second metering unit valve is switched on: if the voltage across the driver stays high, the line evidently has a path to power of less than about 0.5 Ohm.
s: Check engine light on immediately
Long cranking or no start
Reduced power, sometimes stalling
c: Control wire chafed against a battery-fed wire in the harness
Damaged valve connector with pins touching
Shorted turns in the metering valve coil
Low-side driver in the engine control module faulty

P233D.d: Where the ECM switches the solenoid of fuel pressure regulator B on both sides, the ground-side line is checked under P2294 to P2296 and the feed from the high-side driver under P233D to P233F. P233D is the open-circuit code for that feed.
s: Check engine light on
Rail pressure not controllable, reduced power
Possibly hard starting or stalling
c: Supply wire to the regulator solenoid broken or terminal loose
High-side driver in the engine control module faulty

P233E.d: P233E concerns the feed side of fuel pressure regulator B: the line from the ECM's high-side driver to the solenoid is shorted to ground. GM documents it for its 2025 diesels (table 25OBDG04A); there, regulator B means the rail pressure regulator valve.
s: Check engine light on in the first trip
Reduced power, rail pressure deviation
Hard starting or stalling possible
c: Supply wire to the regulator rubbed through to ground
Regulator solenoid shorted internally or to its housing
Water or corrosion in the regulator connector
High-side driver in the engine control module damaged

P233F.d: P233F is set when the feed line of the fuel pressure regulator B solenoid carries voltage even though the ECM has its high-side driver switched off. GM's 2025 diesel table 25OBDG04A describes this test for the rail pressure regulator valve: in the off state the voltage across the driver should be large; if it is low, the line is fed from elsewhere, as if tied to power through less than half an ohm.
s: Check engine light on in the first trip
Rail pressure too high or unstable
Reduced engine power possible
c: Regulator supply wire touching a battery or ignition feed
Bent or bridged pins in the regulator connector
High-side driver in the engine control module stuck on

P2340.d: P2340 reports knock above threshold for cylinder 5, so it can only occur on engines with at least five cylinders – inline-five, six-cylinder, V8 or larger. The principle matches the rest of the series: the module evaluates the knock sensor signal in the crank-angle window of each combustion and retards spark individually when one cylinder knocks.
s: Check engine light on
Pinging or knocking under load
Less power, higher consumption
c: Carbon deposits or glowing particles in cylinder 5
Injector of cylinder 5 delivering too little
Wrong heat range or damaged spark plug

P2341.d: Cylinder 6 is the last cylinder of inline-six and V6 engines, and P2341 reports that its share of the knock sensor signal has crossed the limit. Modern knock control adjusts ignition timing for every cylinder on its own, so a single cylinder can run retarded while the others keep optimum spark; the code tells which one keeps knocking.
s: MIL on
Knocking at full throttle or uphill
Reduced power
c: Fuel octane too low for the engine
Deposits in the combustion chamber of cylinder 6
Loose component or valve train noise read as knock
Lean mixture in cylinder 6 from a restricted injector

P2342.d: P2342 applies only to engines with seven or more cylinders, in practice V8s and larger. It says the vibration picked up by the knock sensor during cylinder 7's combustion window has exceeded the threshold.
s: Check engine light on
Possibly audible knocking under load
Less power from retarded ignition
c: Loose bracket, heat shield or valve train noise in cylinder 7's window
Deposits or hot spots in cylinder 7
Knock sensor of that bank loose or wrongly torqued

P2343.d: P2343 belongs to cylinder 8, the last cylinder of a V8, and is stored when the knock intensity measured in that cylinder's crank-angle window stays above the calibrated limit. The knock control first answers with spark retard for cylinder 8 alone, and on turbocharged engines it may also lower boost; the code marks that this cylinder keeps knocking.
s: Check engine light on
Pinging or knocking, mostly under load
Reduced power, possibly less boost on turbo engines
c: Wrong plug type or gap in cylinder 8
Cylinder 8 running lean from low injector delivery

P2344.d: A ninth cylinder exists only on V10 and V12 engines, so P2344 is confined to a small group of vehicles: V10s such as Ford's 6.8L Triton in E-Series vans, Super Duty pickups and the Excursion, the Dodge Viper and Ram SRT-10, and performance cars from BMW, Audi and Lamborghini, plus the V12s. The code means the knock control has found the vibration level in cylinder 9's combustion window above the limit and is retardin
s: MIL on
Knocking or pinging under heavy load or towing
Reduced power
c: Deposits or hot spots in cylinder 9
Fuel of too low octane for a high-output engine
Wrong or fouled spark plug in cylinder 9

P2345.d: P2345 is the knock code for cylinder 10, the last cylinder of a V10, so it appears mainly on engines such as Ford's 6.8L Triton truck V10, the Viper V10 used by Dodge, and the V10s of BMW M5/M6, Audi and Lamborghini. It sets when the knock signal belonging to cylinder 10's firing window stays over the calibrated limit; the module then keeps that cylinder's spark retarded.
s: Check engine light on
Pinging when towing or climbing
Loss of power
c: High load, towing or high intake temperature with marginal fuel
Valve train noise interpreted as knock

P2346.d: Cylinders 11 and 12 exist only on V12 engines, for example BMW's V12 in the 7 and 8 Series, Mercedes-Benz's M120 and its successors, and the V12s of Ferrari, Lamborghini and Aston Martin. P2346 reports that cylinder 11 has knocked above the threshold that the knock control allows in its crank-angle window.
s: MIL on
Slight loss of power
Possibly audible pinging
c: Deposits or hot spots in cylinder 11
Fuel below the required octane rating
Disturbed crank or knock sensor signal shifting the cylinder assignment

P2347.d: P2347 ends the per-cylinder knock series that starts with P2336 for cylinder 1; it is the code for cylinder 12 and thus appears only on V12 engines such as those from BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Ferrari or Lamborghini. The engine module has found that the vibration in cylinder 12's combustion window exceeds the threshold and is holding back that cylinder's spark.
s: Check engine light on
Reduced power
Possibly knocking under load
c: Mechanical noise near the sensor of that bank

P2348.d: A cylinder pressure sensor, usually built into the glow plug of a diesel, reports the combustion pressure of one cylinder so the ECM can trim injection for it. P2348 is the general circuit code for the sensor of cylinder 9, meant for modules that do not split faults into low and high.
s: Check engine light on
Often no noticeable change in driving
Possibly slightly harsher combustion noise
c: Sensor or glow plug connector of cylinder 9 loose or corroded
Reference, signal or ground wire damaged

P2349.d: P2349 is the plausibility code for the combustion pressure sensor of cylinder 9: the signal is electrically valid but does not match what the ECM expects for the operating point. CARB requires input sensors to be checked for rationality where feasible, in both directions.
s: Check engine light on
Usually no noticeable driveability change
c: Glow plug seat leaking or plug tightened to wrong torque
Genuinely low compression in cylinder 9 distorting the comparison

P234A.d: P234A means the signal of the cylinder 9 combustion pressure sensor stays below its permitted minimum. No published manufacturer document covers cylinder 9; the closest pattern is the GM-built 2.0 CDTI diesel of the Saab 9-5, whose cylinder 1–4 low codes (P0397 for cylinder 1) set after more than 2 s below threshold with the engine running, checked once per operating cycle, as Type B – the MIL comes on after the seco
s: Check engine light after two trips
Peak pressure reads 0 kPa on the scan tool
Driving behaviour mostly unchanged
c: 5 V reference interrupted or shorted to ground
Sensor in the glow plug defective

P234B.d: P234B is stored when the cylinder 9 combustion pressure sensor signal sits above its upper limit. Nobody documents this cylinder-9 code openly, so the description borrows from the Saab 9-5 diesel (GM 2.0 CDTI): its high codes for cylinders 1–4 (P0398 for cylinder 1) need more than 2 s above threshold with the engine running, are tested once per operating cycle and are Type B.
s: Check engine light after two trips
Peak pressure shows an implausibly high fixed value
No obvious drivability complaint
c: Connector at the cylinder 9 glow plug not plugged in
Sensor ground or signal wire interrupted
Reference or signal wire shorted to voltage

P234C.d: P234C covers a cylinder 9 combustion pressure signal that jumps or briefly drops out instead of staying permanently low or permanently high. As an analogue only the Saab 9-5 diesel (a GM 2.0 CDTI) is published: its erratic codes for cylinders 1–4 (P0399 for cylinder 1) react much faster than the low/high codes, already once the signal has left its window for longer than 0.2 s while the engine runs, and they are Type
s: Check engine light, often coming and going
Fault stored but hard to reproduce in the workshop
c: Intermittent contact at the glow plug connector
Harness rubbing on the cylinder head, breaking contact under vibration
Sensor electronics unstable at high temperature

P234D.d: Unlike the sensor circuit codes, P234D judges the pressure itself: the value measured or modelled for cylinder 9 stays below what the ECM expects, while the sensor is electrically in order. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the cylinder-1 analogue P039A is equally undocumented by code; the description therefore rests on CARB's duty to monitor combustion-sensor engines and on how pressure-sensing glow
s: Check engine light on
Rough running, especially at idle
More smoke and higher fuel consumption
c: Injector of cylinder 9 delivering too little or clogged
Compression loss from valve or piston ring wear
Combustion gas escaping at the glow plug seat

P234E.d: P234E reports that the pressure determined for cylinder 9 exceeds the expected maximum. No manufacturer documents the cylinder-9 code publicly.
s: Warning lamp on, sometimes with misfire codes
Harsh, knocking combustion noise
Loss of power if the cylinder is shut off
c: Engine software misjudging combustion (update available at some makers)
Injector of cylinder 9 leaking or injecting too much

P234F.d: P234F flags that the pressure signal of cylinder 9 changes too little: the rise and fall the ECM expects across each combustion cycle is missing or very small. For cylinder 9 there is no manufacturer documentation.
s: Check engine light on
Usually no change in engine behaviour
c: Sensing element of the glow plug stuck by carbon
Cylinder 9 builds up little pressure (compression or injection fault)

P2350.d: P2350 is the opposite of P234F: the cylinder 9 pressure signal swings more than plausible, with peaks or steps that do not fit the engine's operating state. No manufacturer publishes the code for cylinder 9.
s: Check engine light on
Usually no noticeable symptoms
c: Interference or chafing on the sensor signal wire
Sensor electronics in the glow plug failing
Injector of cylinder 9 dribbling after closing

P2351.d: P2351 does not concern the sensor but the quality of combustion in cylinder 9, as judged from the pressure trace: the energy released per cycle, or its balance against the other cylinders, falls outside the permitted window. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, nor its cylinder-1 analogue P039E.
s: Check engine light on
Uneven running and vibration
Increased smoke and fuel consumption
c: Injector of cylinder 9 coked, leaking or sticking
Poor fuel quality or water in the fuel

P2352.d: P2352 is the catch-all code for the electrical circuit of the cylinder 10 combustion pressure sensor, meant for engine computers that make no distinction between low and high. A tenth cylinder exists only on V10 and V12 engines.
s: Check engine light on
Engine usually runs as before
Combustion noise may become slightly harder
c: Glow plug/sensor connector of cylinder 10 not fully latched or corroded
Harness branch to the rear cylinder of the bank chafed or heat-damaged
Electronics in the pressure-sensing glow plug failed

P2353.d: P2353 means the cylinder 10 pressure sensor delivers a signal that is electrically within limits but not believable for the current operating point – the reading is skewed, not cut off. CARB expects input sensors to be checked for such rationality faults, not just for open or shorted circuits.
s: Check engine light on
No noticeable change in engine behaviour
c: Sensor offset drifted with age and heat
Carbon on the heater rod hampers pressure transfer to the diaphragm
Replacement glow plug with calibration for another engine

P2354.d: P2354 reports that the signal of the cylinder 10 pressure sensor stays below its lower limit. The pattern known for this fault type comes from Saab's 9-5 diesel with its GM 2.0 engine: its low codes for the four cylinders (P0397 on cylinder 1) demand that a running engine sees the signal under the threshold for longer than 2 s, run once per trip and are Type B, so the MIL waits for a second failed trip.
s: Check engine light after the second faulty trip
Scan tool shows peak pressure near zero for cylinder 10
Driving behaviour normally unchanged
c: Signal wire shorted to ground, e.g. chafed on the cylinder head
5 V reference interrupted or shorted to ground
Internal fault of the pressure-sensing glow plug

P2355.d: P2355 means the cylinder 10 pressure signal is stuck above its upper limit. Taking the Saab 9-5 diesel with GM's 2.0 engine as the model, the Type B high codes for its four cylinders (P0398 on cylinder 1) wait until the signal has stayed above the threshold for over 2 s with the engine running.
s: Check engine light after two trips
Peak pressure for cylinder 10 frozen at a very high value
No obvious driveability complaint
c: Signal or low reference wire open, connector pulled off
Signal or reference shorted to a voltage source
Sensor electronics driving the output high

P2356.d: P2356 points to a cylinder 10 pressure signal that drops out or jumps for moments instead of failing permanently. No manufacturer covers cylinder 10 publicly.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Fault hard to reproduce in the workshop
c: Connector not fully seated, contact lost under vibration
Wire break inside the insulation or chafe point that opens intermittently
Glow plug sensor electronics failing intermittently

P2357.d: P2357 is not about the wiring: the pressure measured or modelled for cylinder 10 itself is below expectation while the sensor circuit tests fine. No manufacturer publishes this code, and the cylinder-1 counterpart P039A is equally undocumented.
s: Check engine light on
Rough running, mainly at idle
More smoke and higher fuel consumption
c: Injector of cylinder 10 delivering too little fuel
Compression loss from valve leakage or worn rings
Combustion gas leaking past the glow plug seal

P2358.d: P2358 indicates that the pressure determined for cylinder 10 exceeds its upper expectation. No manufacturer documents this cylinder-10 code.
s: Warning lamp on, sometimes together with misfire codes
Hard, knocking combustion noise
Reduced power if the cylinder is switched off
c: Engine control software misjudging combustion (update available)
Injector of cylinder 10 leaking or over-delivering

P2359.d: P2359 means the pressure trace of cylinder 10 changes too little: the build-up through compression and combustion is flatter than the ECM expects. No manufacturer documents this code for cylinder 10.
s: Check engine light on
Engine behaviour usually unchanged
c: Heater rod stuck in carbon, pressure no longer reaches the diaphragm
Cylinder 10 builds up hardly any pressure

P235A.d: P235A is the counterpart to P2359: the cylinder 10 pressure signal swings more than the combustion can explain, with spikes or steps from one cycle to the next. A public manufacturer description of this tenth-cylinder code does not exist.
s: Check engine light on
Usually no noticeable symptoms
c: Interference on a damaged or poorly shielded signal wire
Poor engine ground or corroded ground point
Sensor electronics delivering an unstable signal
Injector dribbling after closing, combustion varies

P235B.d: P235B rates how well cylinder 10 burns, derived from its pressure curve – for instance from the energy each working cycle releases or from how it compares with the other nine cylinders of a V10. No manufacturer documents this code, nor the cylinder-1 equivalent P039E.
s: Check engine light on
Uneven running and vibration
Increased smoke and fuel consumption
c: Coked or worn injector of cylinder 10
Air leak in the intake tract

P235C.d: P235C stands for a fault in the circuit of the cylinder 11 combustion pressure sensor without saying whether the signal is too low or too high. A V10 ends at cylinder 10, so only twelve-cylinder engines have an eleventh one.
s: Check engine light on
No change in how the engine runs
c: Connector at the cylinder 11 glow plug loose or corroded
Reference, low reference or signal wire damaged
Sensor electronics in the glow plug failed

P235D.d: P235D is set when the combustion pressure reported for cylinder 11 is electrically valid yet does not fit the engine's state – for example a compression peak that is clearly off while no fuel is being injected. Only engines with twelve cylinders have a cylinder 11, and none of them is publicly documented with pressure sensors, so no manufacturer describes this code.
s: Check engine light on
Driving behaviour practically unchanged
c: Glow plug with calibration for another engine application fitted
Deposits on the heater rod distort the reading
Seal at the glow plug seat leaking

P235E.d: With P235E the signal of the cylinder 11 combustion pressure sensor is too low, typically close to zero. No manufacturer documents this code, as twelve-cylinder engines with pressure sensors are not described publicly; the analogue is P0397 for cylinder 1 in Saab's 9-5 diesel, where a low signal must persist beyond 2 s with the engine running before the Type B code is logged.
s: Warning lamp after the second faulty trip
Peak pressure of cylinder 11 shown as zero
c: 5 V reference interrupted or shorted to ground
Signal wire chafed through to ground
Sensor glow plug outside its 3–12 Ohm specification

P235F.d: P235F is logged when the cylinder 11 pressure sensor signal remains above its plausible maximum. Only twelve-cylinder engines have this cylinder, and no maker documents the code; the Saab 9-5 diesel serves as the model with P0398 for cylinder 1, a Type B code that needs more than 2 s over the threshold.
s: Check engine light after two trips
Implausibly high fixed pressure value for cylinder 11
c: Low reference (ground) wire of the sensor open
Signal wire interrupted or connector off
Reference or signal shorted to battery voltage
Insulation failure between sensor terminals and plug body

P2360.d: P2360 records a cylinder 11 combustion pressure signal that is unsteady – brief dropouts or spikes that do not last long enough for a low or high code. Since only twelve-cylinder engines have cylinder 11, and none is documented with pressure sensors, the code has no public manufacturer description.
s: Check engine light that comes and goes
Fault stored without a lasting complaint
c: Fretting corrosion or loose fit at the connector terminals
Sensor electronics in the plug head failing when warm

P2361.d: P2361 says the combustion pressure of cylinder 11 is too low although the sensor works electrically. No manufacturer documents this code, since no twelve-cylinder engine with combustion pressure sensing is publicly described.
s: Check engine light on
Uneven running, especially at idle
Possibly misfire code for cylinder 11 as well
c: Injector of cylinder 11 with reduced flow or clogged nozzle
Worn piston rings or burnt valve lowering compression
Leak at the glow plug seat

P2362.d: P2362 is stored when cylinder 11 shows more combustion pressure than the ECM considers plausible. No manufacturer publishes it, because no twelve-cylinder engine with cylinder pressure monitoring is documented.
s: Warning lamp on
Harsh combustion noise
Loss of power if the cylinder is shut off
c: Injector of cylinder 11 leaking or hanging open
Injection timing too early for this cylinder
Engine control software misjudging the pressure

P2363.d: P2363 flags a cylinder 11 pressure signal with too little swing between its low point and the combustion peak. No manufacturer documents this code; cylinder 11 only exists on twelve-cylinder engines, none of which is publicly known with pressure-sensing glow plugs.
s: Check engine light on
Engine runs normally in most cases
c: Piezo-resistive sensing element has lost sensitivity
Deposits holding the heater rod in place

P2364.d: P2364 is stored when the pressure signal of cylinder 11 varies too strongly, from cycle to cycle or within one cycle. No maker publishes this code.
s: Check engine light on
No noticeable effect on driving
c: Interference coupling into the signal line
Ground connection with changing contact resistance
Moisture in the glow plug connector

P2365.d: P2365 means the ECM judges combustion in cylinder 11 to be poor, based on the pressure signal rather than on crankshaft speed alone. No manufacturer publishes this code; twelve-cylinder engines with pressure-sensing glow plugs are not documented.
s: Check engine light on
Uneven running and vibration
More smoke from the exhaust
c: Fouled or leaking injector of cylinder 11

P2366.d: P2366 is the general circuit code for the combustion pressure sensor of cylinder 12; it does not tell whether the signal sits too low or too high. Twelve is the highest number on a V12 or W12.
s: Check engine light on
Pressure reading for cylinder 12 missing or fixed in live data
c: Glow plug connector not fully latched or loose
Damaged wire in the harness branch to the rearmost cylinder

P2367.d: With P2367 the cylinder 12 pressure signal is electrically within its limits but makes no sense for the operating point. A natural yardstick is the motored cycle: on overrun nothing burns, so the curve has to peak at top dead centre.
s: Check engine light on
Implausible peak pressure value for cylinder 12 compared with the others
c: Sensor zero point or gain drifted
Combustion gas escaping at the glow plug seat
Glow plug of a different calibration fitted

P2368.d: P2368 is stored when the voltage coming from the cylinder 12 pressure sensor stays below its lower limit. As the last cylinder of a V12 or W12, it has no publicly documented application, so Saab's 9-5 diesel code P0397 serves as the template.
s: Warning lamp after two trips with the fault
Peak pressure of cylinder 12 stuck near zero
c: 5 V reference open or shorted to ground
Sensor electronics in the glow plug head failed low

P2369.d: P2369 means the cylinder 12 pressure input reads above its upper limit. Like the rest of the cylinder-12 family, it is not documented publicly by any maker.
s: Check engine light after the second trip
Cylinder 12 shows an impossibly high pressure in live data
c: Signal shorted to a voltage source
Glow plug sensor electronics outputting a fixed high value

P236A.d: P236A covers brief, irregular disturbances of the cylinder 12 pressure signal – faults that come and go without settling into a lasting low or high state. Its model is the Saab 9-5 diesel code P0399, which responds as soon as the signal stays outside its band longer than 0.2 s.
s: Warning lamp that switches on and off over several days
Pressure value of cylinder 12 jumps when the harness is moved
c: Loose or corroded terminal in the plug connector
Harness rubbing through under engine vibration
Glow plug sensor with intermittent internal fault

P236B.d: P236B reports that cylinder 12 builds too little combustion pressure while its sensor circuit itself is in order. No manufacturer documents the code, because no V12 or W12 with cylinder pressure measurement has been made public.
s: Check engine light on
Rough idle and vibration
Misfire code for cylinder 12 stored as well
c: Intake or exhaust valve of cylinder 12 not sealing
Worn piston rings or head gasket leak
Gas leaking past the glow plug seal

P236C.d: P236C flags combustion pressure in cylinder 12 above its allowed value. A public twelve-cylinder application does not exist.
s: EPC or check engine lamp on
Loss of power when the cylinder is switched off
Harder combustion noise
c: Injector dripping or delivering too much pilot fuel

P236D.d: P236D is stored when the cylinder 12 pressure trace swings too little – the curve stays flatter than compression and combustion ought to make it. No manufacturer documents this code for a twelve-cylinder engine.
s: Check engine light on
Flat pressure curve for cylinder 12 in live data
c: Carbon deposits restricting the heater rod

P236E.d: P236E means the pressure signal of cylinder 12 scatters more than the ECM tolerates, either within one cycle or from one cycle to the next. No manufacturer publishes the code; the reference is Saab's P039D for cylinder 1, a Type B fault that needs only 0.2 s outside its window.
s: Check engine light on
Occasional slight roughness
c: Injector delivery varying from shot to shot

P236F.d: P236F is the ECM's verdict that combustion in cylinder 12 falls short, judged from the evaluated pressure curve rather than from a single limit. No manufacturer documents it, as no twelve-cylinder engine with cylinder pressure sensing is public.
s: Check engine light on
Rough running
More visible exhaust smoke
c: Injector of cylinder 12 coked or worn

P2370.d: A fuel volume regulator is the solenoid valve at the high-pressure pump that decides how much of the pump's stroke reaches the rail. Regulator B only exists where a second valve or second pump is fitted – the 5.2 litre V10 of Audi and Lamborghini, for instance, has two cam-driven high-pressure pumps for its two rails.
s: Check engine light on
Rail pressure deviation and possible reduced power
Hard starting
c: Connector at regulator B loose or corroded

P2371.d: P2371 is a functional fault of the second fuel volume regulator: the control circuit works electrically, but the valve does not achieve what the ECM asks of it. No manufacturer publishes a definition for regulator B, so the A side helps.
s: Check engine light on
Rail pressure fluctuates or misses its target
Reduced power under load
c: Regulator B valve sticking from dirt or wear

P2372.d: P2372 says the line driving fuel volume regulator B is pulled too low, as a rule by contact with ground. No manufacturer documents this B code publicly; it mirrors P0003 on regulator A.
s: Check engine light on
Rail pressure too high or too low depending on the affected side
Limp-home with reduced power
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Internal short in the regulator coil

P2373.d: P2373 points to too much voltage or current in the control circuit of fuel volume regulator B, typically from a short to battery voltage or a shorted coil. No manufacturer publishes the B version; P0004 on regulator A is the model.
s: Check engine light on
Reduced power or limp-home mode
Rail pressure deviation codes stored as well
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Regulator coil with shorted turns drawing excess current

P2374.d: P2374 covers any wiring or sensor-side failure of a second pressure sensor mounted upstream of a compressor. Where the letter B belongs is the manufacturer's choice; on parallel twin-turbo V engines, where each turbocharger serves one cylinder bank, a second inlet sensor for the other compressor is the obvious candidate.
s: Check engine light on
Reduced boost or power
c: Connector or wire of sensor B open, corroded or shorted
Sensor B reports an internal error

P2375.d: With P2375 the signal of compressor inlet pressure sensor B is electrically valid but implausible – stuck, offset or out of step with the other pressure values. No manufacturer publishes the B code; GM's 2018 table for the supercharged LT4 V8 describes the A counterpart P012B in detail.
s: Check engine light after two trips
Uneven boost between the two turbochargers
Reduced power
c: Air filter on the side of compressor B clogged
Leaking or collapsed duct ahead of compressor B

P2376.d: P2376 is set when the output voltage of compressor inlet pressure sensor B drops below its lower limit. No maker documents the B code publicly; GM's A version P012C on the supercharged LT4 gives an idea of the scale.
s: Check engine light on
Live data show an inlet pressure far below ambient
Possible boost limitation
c: Signal wire of sensor B shorted to ground
5 V reference to sensor B open

P2377.d: P2377 means sensor B ahead of the compressor delivers a voltage above its upper limit. Publicly no manufacturer defines this B code, so GM's P012D for the supercharged LT4 serves as a reference: it trips above 97 % of the 5 V reference, which equals about 124 kPa at that sensor, again with 320 failed samples out of 400 at 12.5 ms intervals and Type B.
s: Check engine light on
Implausibly high inlet pressure in live data
c: Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Sensor ground of sensor B open
Moisture bridging terminals in the connector

P2378.d: P2378 records a signal from compressor inlet pressure sensor B that jumps or briefly drops out without staying beyond a limit. No manufacturer documents it publicly, and even for the A sensor a dedicated erratic code is rare: GM's LT4 table catches short spikes only through the counting window of its low and high checks (320 of 400 samples), and Ford's 2023 diesels fold faults of their digital sensor into P012A.
s: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief hesitation under boost
c: Harness damaged by heat from the turbocharger

P2379.d: P2379 covers the oxygen sensor behind the catalyst on bank 2 at the moment the injectors are shut off on a closed throttle: the exhaust is then close to fresh air, and a sensor whose reading stays outside the expected lean window is suspect. No manufacturer documents P2379 publicly.
s: Check engine light on
No noticeable change in how the car drives
Downstream O2 reading on bank 2 stays high during coasting in live data
c: Bank 2 downstream sensor aged or contaminated, reacting too little to fuel cut
Exhaust leak near the bank 2 rear sensor diluting or distorting the sample
Chafed sensor lead or corroded connector on the bank 2 rear sensor
Leaking injector on bank 2 keeping fuel in the exhaust during overrun

P237A.d: P237A says the rear oxygen sensor of bank 1 is not getting, or not reporting, a representative sample of exhaust: its reading does not fit the gas that should be flowing past it after the catalyst, typically because outside air enters through a leak or the sensing element is no longer exposed properly. No manufacturer documents P237A publicly.
s: Check engine light on
Catalyst monitor not completing or reporting implausible results
Possible ticking exhaust noise from a leak
c: Leak at a flange, joint or cracked pipe ahead of the bank 1 rear sensor drawing in air
Rear sensor element damaged, coated or loose in its boss
Contaminated or blocked reference air path of the sensor (wiring or connector)

P237B.d: P237B is the bank 2 version of the sample check on the post-catalyst oxygen sensor and therefore only appears on engines with two exhaust banks, mostly V6 and V8 units with a separate downstream sensor on each side. The ECM decides that what the sensor reports cannot be genuine exhaust from that bank, for example because a leak at the second-bank pipe lets air in or the probe is mounted badly.
s: Check engine light on
Bank 2 catalyst monitor incomplete or failing
Engine runs as usual
c: Air leak in the bank 2 exhaust between catalyst and rear sensor
Bank 2 rear sensor damaged, poisoned or not seated correctly
Rear sensors of bank 1 and bank 2 swapped at the connectors after a repair

P237C.d: Some hybrids route the exhaust through a coolant heat exchanger after a cold start to warm the engine and cabin sooner, and flap A sends the gas around it once heat is no longer wanted. P237C is set when the drive circuit of that bypass actuator shows an open or a general circuit fault.
s: Check engine light on
Engine and cabin may warm up more slowly in cold weather
Further heat exchanger codes such as P2C22 stored alongside
c: Water inside the heat exchanger assembly or actuator (Ford Maverick SSM 51921)
Bypass valve actuator with open winding or failed electronics
Broken wire or loose connector in the hot area under the vehicle

P237D.d: P237D concerns the same drive line as P237C, the one that operates bypass flap A of an exhaust heat recovery unit, but here the module measures a voltage that sits too low – the usual picture of a control wire touching ground or an actuator shorted internally. Moisture in a connector under the car can produce exactly that.
s: Check engine light on
Slower heater response after a cold start
Car otherwise drives normally
c: Water in the heat exchanger or its actuator shorting the drive (Maverick)
Control wire chafed through against the body or exhaust bracket

P237E.d: P237E is logged when the driver for exhaust bypass flap A on a heat recovery unit sees a control voltage above its expected range. The likely story is a short from the control wire to a supply feed or an actuator whose internal driver has failed in a way that pulls the line up.
s: Check engine light on
Cabin heat may build up later on cold days
c: Heat exchanger bypass actuator with failed internal driver (Ford F-150 SSM 53003)
Control wire shorted to a supply circuit in the harness

P237F.d: P237F is not about wiring of the drive but about the result: the bypass flap A of the exhaust heat recovery unit was commanded, yet the effect the module expects does not appear. Ford judges this partly by temperatures, which is why SSM 52543 for the full hybrids F-150 3.5L (from 2021), Explorer 3.3L and Escape 2.5L (from 2020) and Maverick 2.5L (from 2022), all through 2024, first sends technicians to the connectors
s: Check engine light on
No effect on drivability
Often stored together with P2C23
c: Water, corrosion or torn seal at the exhaust coolant temperature sensor 3/4 connectors (Ford SSM 52543)
PCM calibration setting the code falsely (2024 Maverick, TSB 24-2173)
Bypass actuator or flap sluggish, sticking or worn

P2380.d: P2380 is the general circuit code for EGR sensor D. Which sensor carries the letter D is up to the maker.
s: Check engine light on
EGR monitor not completed
Possibly slight knock tendency or higher NOx with EGR reduced
c: Internal fault reported by the smart EGR pressure sensor
Corroded or loose connector at the sensor
Unstable supply or ground to the sensor

P2381.d: P2381 means the signal of EGR sensor D is stuck at the top of its electrical range. GM's 2025 diesel ECM tables use it for the differential pressure sensor of the low-pressure EGR loop: if the raw voltage exceeds 99.83 % of the scale in 480 out of 600 samples, taken every 6.25 ms after cranking and with the powertrain relay above 11 V, GM records a Type A fault, lighting the MIL in the first trip.
s: Check engine light on immediately
Low-pressure EGR disabled, NOx emissions rise
Other harness-related codes possible at the same time
c: Open sensor ground or reference return
Chafed engine harness shorting the signal to a supply (GM 21-NA-149)
Differential pressure sensor failed with output at full scale

P2382.d: P2382 reports that EGR sensor D delivers almost no signal voltage. In GM's 2025 diesel ECM tables this sensor measures the pressure difference across the low-pressure EGR path, and the code sets once the raw value drops below 0.02 % of range in 480 of 600 samples, sampled every 6.25 ms once the engine is out of cranking and the relay supply exceeds 11 V; it is a Type A fault with MIL on the first trip.
s: Check engine light on in the first trip
Low-pressure EGR switched off
Fault may come and go with engine vibration
c: Conductor broken right at the sensor connector (GM 21-NA-149)
Open 5 V reference or signal shorted to ground

P2383.d: P2383 flags an EGR sensor D whose signal is electrically fine but makes no sense. Two published strategies show how differently makers test it.
s: Check engine light on
EGR rate reduced or switched off
Often appears after work on the EGR or exhaust system
c: Sensor hoses swapped, cracked or disconnected (Ford EGRP)
Sensor drifted so that it reads a pressure difference with the engine off (GM)
Sensing lines blocked by soot or condensate
Intermittent wire break at the sensor connector (GM 21-NA-149)

P2384.d: P2384 marks an EGR sensor D signal that jumps or drops out for brief moments without staying at a fixed fault level. GM's 2025 diesel ECM tables apply it to the differential pressure sensor of the low-pressure EGR loop: when two successive raw readings differ by more than 10 % in 300 out of 600 samples, taken every 6.25 ms with the relay supply above 11 V and no high or low circuit fault present, a Type A fault is lo
s: MIL on, often without noticeable driving change
Code stored, cleared and returning after some drives
EGR operation reduced as a precaution
c: Loose or corroded terminals at the EGR sensor D connector
Harness chafing intermittently on engine or exhaust parts
Sensor with an internal contact fault

P2385.d: P2385 is the general circuit code for a fifth EGR-related sensor, labelled E. The letter is assigned by each manufacturer, so the code only makes sense on engines with an extensive set of EGR sensors, such as diesels that pair high- and low-pressure loops with several pressure and temperature probes.
s: MIL on
EGR monitor not completing, readiness stays open
Possibly higher NOx and slightly changed engine response under load
c: Connector of EGR sensor E unplugged, damaged or corroded
Open or shorted wire between sensor and engine control unit

P2386.d: P2386 says the signal of EGR sensor E sits at or above the upper end of its electrical range. With a typical three-wire 5 V pressure or position sensor that happens when the ground is open or the signal line touches a supply voltage; on a temperature sensor wired as a pull-up, an open circuit shows the same picture.
s: MIL on
EGR shut off or reduced
Scan data shows sensor E at full scale
c: Open sensor ground wire or ground terminal
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage

P2387.d: P2387 is stored when the signal of EGR sensor E falls below its valid electrical range. On a pressure sensor with a 5 V reference that typically points to a lost reference feed, a signal wire shorted to ground or a sensor that no longer drives its output; a shorted thermistor would produce the same result on a temperature input.
s: MIL on
Further low-voltage codes on sensors sharing the same reference
EGR in fallback mode
c: 5 V reference open or pulled down by another sensor

P2388.d: P2388 covers an EGR sensor E whose signal is electrically valid but does not agree with what the engine controller expects from the operating state. Typical tests compare the reading with a known condition, such as zero pressure difference with the engine off, or with a modelled value from other sensors.
s: MIL on
EGR monitor readiness not set
Sensor E reading implausible at engine off
c: Sensing hoses blocked, cracked or swapped
Soot deposits at the sensor port

P2389.d: P2389 points to an EGR sensor E signal that is mostly plausible but now and then jumps, spikes or drops out. Engine controllers detect this by watching the rate of change between consecutive readings rather than absolute limits.
s: MIL on, sometimes going out again
Fault cannot be reproduced at the workshop
Jumps visible in the sensor E data stream
c: Weak pin tension or unlatched connector
Harness damaged by heat or rubbing near the exhaust
Sensor with an intermittent internal fault

P238A.d: P238A is the general circuit code for water-in-fuel sensor B, used where a diesel has two water-detecting points, for example a frame-mounted primary filter and a second separator. Stellantis case file S2214000004 for 2022 Ram 2500 to 5500 trucks shows that on these vehicles the B sensor is part of the fuel filter mounted on the frame; P238A itself is not named there.
s: Water-in-fuel lamp or message on
No warning for real water in the chassis filter
c: Water or corrosion in the sensor B connector at the chassis filter
Damaged harness along the frame rail

P238B.d: P238B means water-in-fuel sensor B delivers a signal that is electrically valid but implausible, for instance a value stuck between the clear dry and wet states, or a self-test answer that arrives at the wrong moment. No manufacturer documents P238B publicly.
s: Water-in-fuel warning without water being found
Warning that persists after draining
c: Dirt film or deposits on the sensor electrodes
Residual water or emulsion around the probe after incomplete draining

P238C.d: P238C is set when the signal line of water-in-fuel sensor B stays below its valid range. Because the sensor reads conductivity, anything that bridges its terminals or pulls the signal to ground can cause it: a chafed wire, a wet connector or a sensor body full of water.
s: Water-in-fuel lamp on
Fault appears after washing or rain
c: Water bridging the terminals in the sensor connector
Signal wire chafed through to ground on the frame

P238D.d: P238D reports that the signal of water-in-fuel sensor B sits above its valid range, usually from an open circuit, a disconnected sensor or a short to voltage. Stellantis case file S2214000004 documents it for 2022 Ram 2500, 3500, 4500 and 5500 trucks: the water warning lamp or message comes on at low mileage, and the cause is water that a pressure washer or similar spray drove into the plug of the filter housing on t
s: Water-in-fuel lamp or message on at low mileage
No water found when draining
c: Spray water in the connector at the chassis-mounted fuel filter
Corroded terminals on harness or filter housing side
Sensor in the filter housing failed

P238E.d: P238E is meant for a water-in-fuel sensor B circuit whose signal flickers or drops out for short periods instead of staying at one fault level. No manufacturer documents P238E publicly.
s: Water-in-fuel lamp flickering or coming and going
Fault not present when tested at the workshop
c: Moisture entering and drying out in the connector
Loose terminals losing contact on rough roads
Broken harness clips letting the wire rub on the frame

P238F.d: P238F is no wiring fault: it states that water-in-fuel sensor B has detected water, meaning the separator at that point has collected enough to bridge the probe. Ram's 2022 heavy-duty pickups (2500 to 5500) are covered by Stellantis case S2214000004, which keeps it apart from the circuit code P238D: with P238F stored, the filter on the frame has to be emptied completely and the fuel tested for water before any electr
s: Water-in-fuel lamp or message on
Rough running or power loss if water reaches the injection system
MIL on some vehicles
c: Water collected in the chassis filter separator
Fuel contaminated with water from tank or filling station
Separator drained incompletely after an earlier warning

P2390.d: P2390 concerns the drive circuit of the second electronically operated intake throttle that some diesel engines carry; which flap a maker labels A or B is its own choice. With the driver switched off, the engine module checks whether the motor circuit is closed; an open wire, a pulled connector or a burnt motor winding sets this code.
s: MIL on, often without a noticeable change in driving
Particulate filter regeneration delayed or blocked
Engine may shake more when switched off because the flap no longer closes
c: Connector at the B throttle unplugged, loose or with pushed-back terminals
Broken motor lead in the harness between module and throttle
Open motor winding inside the throttle unit
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

P2391.d: P2391 compares where the B intake throttle should be with where its position sensor says it is. If the gap stays too large under a steady command, the module concludes that the flap is sluggish or obstructed, typically by soot and oil deposits from EGR and crankcase gases, a worn gear stage or a weak motor.
s: MIL on
Regeneration of the particulate filter does not complete
Occasionally reduced power or uneven response
c: Soot and oil deposits making the B flap stiff
Worn plastic gears or shaft bearing in the throttle unit
Weak motor or high resistance in the drive circuit
Position sensor reporting an offset angle

P2392.d: P2392 is set when the module finds the motor output for the B intake throttle pulled towards ground, for example by a chafed wire touching the engine, water inside the connector or a shorted motor. The output stage protects itself and switches off.
s: MIL on, code returns immediately after clearing
Regeneration blocked or aborted
Little or no change in driving
c: Motor lead chafed through and touching engine or body ground
Water or corrosion in the throttle connector
Internal short of the throttle motor to its housing
Damaged H-bridge in the engine control module
